items.title: Re-vendor LibKa0s v1.71.0 from the local tag; record the unrecorded v1.69.0/v1.70.0 re-vendors as a span bundle and de-tag the stale library/kit stamps
items.spec:
Mechanical re-vendor per the dev-copilot wow-revendor-libka0s convention, from the LOCAL LibKa0s tag v1.71.0 (../LibKa0s, tag not pushed; OWNER_SCOPE 5).
End state:
- libs/LibKa0s/ is byte-identical to ../LibKa0s's LibKa0s/ payload at v1.71.0 and tests/_kit/ byte-identical to its testkit/ (copy both whole; delete files the tag dropped). Nothing else under libs/ or tests/_kit/ changes.
- CLAUDE.md last line rolls to 'Bundles [LibKa0s](https://github.com/tusharsaxena/LibKa0s) v1.71.0 (MIT).' (the provenance line is the one place a tag is owed).
- MM-A-01 (cluster C03, third firing): new span bundle docs/revendor/<date>-v1.69.0-v1.70.0/ for the bare re-vendor commits 824999b (v1.69.0, kit 37, adds WidgetsLineChart) and 1ee53cf (v1.70.0): 01_DELTA.md whose line 1 is exactly 'Delta: LibKa0s v1.69.0 -> v1.70.0 (span: v1.69.0 v1.70.0)', with the base (v1.68.1, the provenance line before 824999b) and the per-file LibStub minors/kit revision stated in the body; 05_SUMMARY.md with one line per tag: carried by the sweep, nothing adopted, WidgetsLineChart and WidgetsAutocomplete unused by MultiMeters. Match the file set and shape of the newest existing bundle docs/revendor/2026-10-04-v1.68.1/ for anything the convention also requires.
- New docs/revendor/<date>-v1.71.0/ bundle (delta base v1.70.0 from the CLAUDE.md provenance line, never the library's previous tag): per-file minor deltas (WidgetsLineChart 3, WidgetsAutocomplete 2, Slash key 20.2, Env minor 2, OptionsIdList minor 4, kit revision 38 with Kit.secret), which majors MultiMeters consumes, contract changes under unchanged signatures, and a section 'Not adopted in this run' listing every adoption candidate (Kit.secret / the opt-in issecretvalue installer, LineChart and Autocomplete changes as unused surfaces, anything else the delta surfaces) with one line each. No interview, no GitHub issue filing (OWNER_SCOPE 5). Effects the fresh payload brings by itself are recorded there: kit rev 38 '--list' Totals count only cases that run and declared skips get a '| Skipped | N |' row (LK-01); Slash ParseValue now refuses nan/inf (LK-05) for /mm set; Env minor 2 drops the library's own bare-global rung (LK-06; MultiMeters' own library-absent stub rung is MM-07's job).
- MM-A-02: remove the stale tag/kit stamps rather than bumping them (a bumped stamp goes stale on the next re-vendor): docs/settings-panel.md:29 drops 'v1.68.1' (or points at the CLAUDE.md provenance line); docs/testing.md:597 and DEPENDENCIES.md:35 drop '(kit 36)'/'kit 36'. Leave the rest of DEPENDENCIES.md:35 (the lizard pin) for MM-09. tests/_kit/framework.lua is payload: never edit it.
- docs/test-cases.md regenerated with the new kit (lua tests/run.lua --list > docs/test-cases.md) and the README Tests badge set to the new Total if it moved.
- If the new payload turns any test red, adapt THIS addon's stubs/fixtures/tests to the v1.71.0 contract in the same commit (never edit libs/ or tests/_kit/, never weaken an assertion) and say so in the commit body; the commit must end green.
Commit subject: 'RV-MM: re-vendor LibKa0s v1.71.0; record the v1.69.0-v1.70.0 span'.

items.title: Merge pets: an owner's own figures add to a cell its pet created earlier in the column instead of replacing it
items.spec:
Bug (high, must). modules/Aggregator.lua: with Merge pets on (settings/Schema.lua:1247), foldPet's absent-cell branch (~:265-273) creates the owner's cell from the pet's figures via setCell; when the owner's own source arrives later in the same column, placeSource's own path (~:927-928) calls setCell, which replaces row.values[statKey] outright (~:240), losing the pet's numbers. Wrong total, rate, percent and /mm export (modules/Export.lua:292) whenever the pet out-ranks its owner in a column.
End state:
- foldPet's absent-cell branch marks the cell it creates as pet-seeded (e.g. cell.petSeeded = true).
- The own-source write, when it finds a pet-seeded cell for that statKey, adds instead of replacing: total = own + pet, and rate summed when both are numbers, under exactly foldPet's guards (Secrets.CanCompare2(cell.total, src.totalAmount) and both type()=='number'). The owner's maxAmount, deathRecapID and deathTime take the owner's values (and row.deathRecapID promotion is unchanged); the pet-seeded mark is cleared. If the guards refuse (secret operand), the owner's own figures replace the cell as before and the refusal is counted in the same per-pass refusal tally foldPet's refusals use, so it is reported, never approximated.
- The counted-stat (isCount) and deaths paths are unchanged. Owner-before-pet order behaves exactly as today.
- setCell/placeSource stay at or below CCN 15 (extract a small mergeOwnIntoPetSeeded helper if needed); Aggregator.lua stays at or below its current 1308 lines + the helper, under the 1500 cap.
- tests/test_aggregator.lua: NEW case (MM-R-02; do not rewrite the existing order-only case at :341) 'A pet ahead of its owner in a column still sums into the owner' with sources PET 400 -> BETA 200 -> ALPHA 100 (PET owned by ALPHA), mergePets on, out of combat: ALPHA DamageDone.total == 500 and rate == pet rate + owner rate; plus a case where the guard refuses (secret owner total via tests/mock_secrets.lua) asserting the owner's own value is shown and one refusal is counted. '-- red under:' comments (testing-§12) naming the replace-in-setCell behaviour.
- docs/data-flow.md (or wherever the pet fold is described) states the order-independence.
Commit subject: 'MM-01: ...' (finding ids MM-R-01 + MM-R-02 in the body).
items.steps:
1. Red first: add the pet-first case to tests/test_aggregator.lua next to the :305/:320 pet cases; run lua tests/run.lua and see 'expected 500, got 100'.
2. Add the refusal case; see it red or note why it is already green.
3. Implement the pet-seeded mark and the summing own-source write in modules/Aggregator.lua.
4. Check complexity of setCell/placeSource with the kit complexity suite; split if above 15.
5. Update the pet-fold paragraph in docs/data-flow.md / docs/ARCHITECTURE.md if it describes the order.
6. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge.
7. Green gate, commit.

items.title: A partial roster is rebuilt at most once per aggregate pass, not on every lookup
items.spec:
modules/Roster.lua ensure() (~:537-541) returns build() whenever cache.partial is set, and Roster.Get / IsGroupMember / OwnerOf / LocalGUID all call ensure(), so one 7-column Aggregator.Build over a 3-member group with one unresolved unit costs ~60 UnitGUID calls instead of 3, every 0.25 s while the roster stays partial. The comments at :405 and :535 claim one walk per refresh.
End state:
- New public Roster.BeginPass(): arms exactly one retry of a partial roster (e.g. cache.retryArmed = true). ensure() rebuilds when there is no cache.group, or when cache.partial AND the retry is armed; build() disarms. A complete roster is never rebuilt by ensure() (unchanged). Invalidation paths (Roster.Refresh, Roster.Forget, GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE handling) keep their current behaviour.
- modules/Aggregator.lua Build calls Roster.BeginPass() once at the start of the pass, before any lookup, so every later lookup in that pass answers from cache. Callers outside a pass (tooltip, drill-down) read the cache.
- The comments at Roster.lua:405 and :535 say what the code now does (one retry per aggregate pass); the DebugSteady partial-line gating is unchanged.
- tests/test_roster.lua (or test_aggregator.lua): a case that counts UnitGUID calls (or build() runs) during one multi-column Aggregator.Build over a partial roster and asserts one rebuild for the pass (red: today it rebuilds per lookup); a case that a second pass retries again and a completed roster stops retrying. '-- red under:' notes.
- Optional (do it if cheap): an offline 'rosterPartial' scenario in tests/perf.lua beside rosterBurst (performance-§9) and its measured figures in docs/performance.md.
items.steps:
1. Red first: the rebuild-count case; confirm it fails with the per-lookup rebuild count.
2. Add Roster.BeginPass and the armed retry in ensure()/build().
3. Call it at the top of Aggregator.Build.
4. Fix the two comments; optionally add the perf scenario and figures.
5. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and README badge; update docs/module-map.md's Roster exports.
6. Green gate, commit.

items.title: Renaming a window to a different case of its own name keeps the name instead of appending ' 2'
items.spec:
modules/WindowManager.lua: uniqueName(base) (~:187-194) asks M.Resolve, which matches names case-insensitively (~:120-127) and therefore counts the window being renamed as a collision, so Rename 'Raid' -> 'raid' stores 'raid 2' (the panel guard at settings/Windows.lua:290 only catches exact matches).
End state: uniqueName(base, selfId) takes an optional id; a Resolve hit whose cfg.id == selfId is not a collision (both for base and for every 'base N' probe). M:Rename (~:318-330) passes cfg.id; create/duplicate/new callers pass nothing and behave as today. tests/test_windowmanager.lua gains 'Rename to a different case of its own name keeps that name' (Raid -> raid stores 'raid'; renaming to another window's name in a different case still gets ' 2'). '-- red under:' note. docs/slash-dispatch.md or docs/ARCHITECTURE.md only if they describe the uniquing rule.

- The three-place standards reference conforms to the v2.77.0 shape: MultiMeters.toc '## X-Standard', the README Standard badge, and the CLAUDE.md 'Standards compliance' block (today all three are versionless; carry a version only where v2.77.0's documentation/toc rules require one, and match the form the other addons use in this run).
